title: T1055.012 — Process Injection - Process Hollowing
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Process Injection - Process Hollowing with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.
aria: Animated diagram of process hollowing. An attacker loader creates a suspended svchost.exe, unmaps its real image, writes a malicious PE image, fixes the entry point, and resumes the thread. A SOC panel on the right fills with evidence: Sysmon event 1 with a wrong parent, event 10 with process memory write access, unbacked executable memory, and a rare network connection. The defender isolates the host in the final step.

steps.title: Phishing payload lands
steps.caption: The attacker sends an email with a document attachment. The user opens it, and a hidden loader program starts on the Windows host WORKSTATION-42. Evidence: suspicious file created
steps.defender: a suspicious file was created and a new unknown process started. File and process creation events are the first hints.

steps.title: Loader creates svchost.exe suspended
steps.caption: The loader calls CreateProcessW to start svchost.exe with the CREATE_SUSPENDED flag. The real service host program never runs its own code; its main thread is frozen at the start. Evidence: Sysmon E1 - wrong parent
steps.defender: Sysmon Event ID 1 shows svchost.exe starting from a non-services parent. This is a top hollowing signal.

steps.title: Loader unmaps the real image
steps.caption: The loader calls NtUnmapViewOfSection. This removes the real svchost program image from the memory of the new process, leaving space for the payload. Evidence: EDR image unmap hook
steps.defender: EDR (Endpoint Detection and Response) hooks and the ETW (Event Tracing for Windows) Threat Intelligence provider report an image unmap inside a fresh process.

steps.title: Loader writes the malicious PE
steps.caption: The loader uses WriteProcessMemory to copy its own PE (Portable Executable) image into the process: headers first, then sections, with relocations fixed for the new base address. Evidence: Sysmon E10 - VM write 0x1F0FFF
steps.defender: Sysmon Event ID 10 logs PROCESS_VM_WRITE (the 0x20 right inside the broad 0x1F0FFF mask) from the temp-folder loader into svchost.exe.

steps.title: Entry point set, thread resumed
steps.caption: The loader calls SetThreadContext to point the frozen main thread at the payload entry point, then calls ResumeThread. The trusted binary now runs attacker code. Evidence: EDR context rewrite + resume
steps.defender: the EDR flags a thread context rewrite and a resume call on a suspended system binary, plus a memory image mismatch.

steps.title: Attacker code runs from unbacked memory
steps.caption: The hollowed svchost.exe executes the payload from unbacked memory, that is, memory regions with no file on disk behind them. The disk file of svchost.exe is still perfectly clean. Evidence: scan - unbacked RWX region
steps.defender: a memory scan finds executable RWX (read-write-execute) regions with no file backing inside a signed process. Image path and mapped section do not match.

steps.title: Beacon to command and control
steps.caption: The hollowed process beacons to the C2 (command and control) server. On the network it looks like traffic from svchost.exe, but the service group flag is missing and the destination is rare. Evidence: netflow - svchost to C2 (no -k)
steps.defender: svchost.exe without a -k service group argument makes a rare outbound connection. Proxy and EDR network events agree.

steps.title: Defender response
steps.caption: The defender isolates the host, captures memory, runs a pe-sieve style scan, blocks the parent-child lineage for every endpoint, and deploys mitigation policies such as dynamic code prohibition. Evidence: host isolated, memory captured
steps.defender: containment confirmed. The host is isolated, memory is captured for forensics, and the loader lineage is blocked everywhere else.
